campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 20, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Campbell City Council meeting listed several recognitions, a routine consent calendar, a public hearing on extending deadlines for future phases of the Pruneyard Center project, and a proposed equipment lease for the city's street-marking work. It also listed the Youth Commission's introduction and a request to approve about $2.75 million in bills and claims.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a public hearing on a request from the Pruneyard Center Association to extend the deadlines for Phases 3 and 4 (including a five-story office building, parking structure expansions, and additional commercial buildings) and the related parcel map to December 31, 2031.
The agenda listed a proposed five-year, $159,327 lease with NCL Government Capital, through Sourcewell, for a Thermoplastic Melter Trailer TPM-1500.

Presentations and proclamations listed: Code Enforcement Officer Appreciation Week, recognition of the Campbell Little League Senior All-Star Team as 2026 Northern California Senior League State Championship winners, and an introduction of the 2026-2027 Youth Commission and its initial work plan.
The consent calendar listed approval of bills and claims totaling $2,750,402.16 and a resolution adopting the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 classification and salary schedules.
The consent calendar also listed approval of minutes from several meetings, including special, executive session, and regular meetings dated July 9 through October 6, 2026.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026 Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and bill payments, along with final approvals for two property splits. It also listed an annual update to the City Code and a proposal to start the process of creating a Climate Resilience District.
keyTopics: Final approval of a map splitting the property at 14860 Farwell Ave into two lots
Final approval of a map splitting the property at 18510 Sobey Rd into two lots
Annual update to the City Code, with a public hearing on changes covering scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners, among other provisions
Resolutions to create a Climate Resilience District Task Force and to begin the process of establishing a Climate Resilience District
Routine items: approving minutes from the September 30 special meeting and October 7 meeting, and accepting vendor payment registers for 10/01 and 10/08

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026 Los Altos City Council meeting listed a mix of routine approvals and several items with direct impact on the city, including a park expansion contract, a new police backup generator, and a proposed raise for the City Manager. It also listed a temporary moratorium on certain detention or custodial facilities and a presentation from Cal Water on water conservation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract of up to $166,225 with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco to complete the Building B Park Expansion Project, plus up to 10% extra for construction contingencies.
The agenda listed a $417,400 contract with ELECCO of Milpitas to replace the Police Department's backup generator, with up to 15% construction contingency.

The agenda listed an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting an annual base salary of $375,000 effective July 5, 2026, along with a yearly CPI/general salary adjustment provision starting July 2027.
The agenda listed an interim urgency ordinance to extend Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium related to detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities.

The agenda listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures, a resolution approving a Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of the VTA, and a resolution to purchase three replacement maintenance vehicles and one piece of equipment.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine housekeeping items, including approval of minutes from two October 6 meetings and review of the town's August 2026 financial reports. It also listed several items authorizing the Town Manager to sign or amend agreements, including one with Foster and Foster and a three-year agreement, and to negotiate an amendment to a lease.
keyTopics: Approval of the minutes from the October 6, 2026 Special Meeting and the October 6, 2026 regular Town Council Meeting
Receipt of the August 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports and the Monthly Financial and Investment Report for August 2026
Approval and ratification of the accounts payable check registers and payroll report
Authorizing the Town Manager to execute a first amendment with Foster and Foster
Authorizing the Town Manager to negotiate and execute an amendment to a lease, and to enter into a three-year agreement

san-jose.title: San José City Council — October 27, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026 San José City Council meeting listed a mix of labor contracts, city service agreements, park and housing items, and changes to local rules on trash and water use. Items before the Council included new three-year agreements with several city employee groups and a grant for overnight warming locations.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of the terms of three-year agreements (July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2029) with city employee groups, including the Municipal Employees' Federation (AFSCME Local 101) and the engineers, architects, maintenance supervisory, and management associations (IFPTE Local 21).
A grant agreement with HomeFirst Services of Santa Clara County for city-designated overnight warming locations was listed for consideration.

Proposed changes to the city's municipal code covering solid waste management (Chapter 9.10) and a new rule implementing state law on using drinking-quality water to irrigate nonfunctional turf (Chapter 15.10).
Park-related items included actions on the Elia Park project and the renaming of Plaza de César Chávez Park.

Other listed items included amendments to contracts with ALCLEAR, LLC (concession) and Universal Protection Security Systems (video/TV support and maintenance), a Vehicle Abatement Audit Report, and moving the Parkmoor Community Apartments to permanent financing.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 27, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council's October 27, 2026 agenda listed a closed session on City Attorney employment matters, followed by a regular session with youth and awareness recognitions, several housing, development, and transportation items, and a public art strategy. The agenda also listed a presentation from the Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District and time for public comment on items not on the agenda.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a closed session at 5:15 p.m. on labor negotiations and the public employee appointment for the City Attorney position.
The agenda listed an amendment to the LinkedIn development agreement covering 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue (second reading).
The agenda listed tax-exempt bond financing for a multi-family housing project at 334 San Antonio Road.
The agenda listed the design concept for the State Route 237 and Middlefield Road interchange improvements (Project 19-65).
The agenda listed pre-qualification of responsible bidders and subcontractors for the Public Safety Building (Project 20-49) and adoption of a Public Art Strategy.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 27, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda listed a 6 p.m. closed session followed by a 7 p.m. regular Council meeting that included a recognition of World Town Planning Day, routine approvals, and several public hearing and general business items. Items before the Council included a nearly $3.26 million homeless services contract extension, a $7.4 million fire truck purchase, new school speed zones, and changes to local housing rules to match state law.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract extension with WeHOPE for street outreach, the temporary hotel program, mobile hygiene services, and the inclement weather hotel program, with a total not-to-exceed amount of $3,255,267.36, a term through September 10, 2027, and a $2,152,098 budget modification.
The agenda listed a $7,372,642.10 purchase order to Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. for three Pierce 100-foot tower fire apparatuses.
The agenda listed a resolution to establish 15 mph school zones and extend the school zone near Laurelwood Elementary School.
The agenda listed adoption of an ordinance prohibiting the use of drinking-quality (potable) water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, implementing state law AB 1572.

The agenda listed a public hearing on replacing the city's rules for Dual Urban Opportunity (DUO) housing and Urban Lot Splits, along with other zoning and fee code changes to conform with new state laws.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the Cupertino City Council's October 20, 2026 meeting listed a 6:45 PM regular session with several proclamations, a routine consent calendar, two public hearings, and one action item about leasing a city-owned commercial property. A special meeting with a study session was also noticed for 5:45 PM the same evening at Community Hall.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposal to accept $850,000 in federal grant funds and award a design services agreement to Biggs Cardoza Associates, Inc. (up to $1,278,700) for the McClellan Road Bridge Project.

The agenda listed a public hearing on updating the Health and Safety chapter of the General Plan, plus related appendices on community noise and geologic and seismic hazards and a new background report.
The agenda listed a proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard.
The agenda listed a contract with Bay Aerials Gymnastics for city gymnastics classes and camps (up to $480,000, extendable for two more years to a five-year total of up to $800,000).

The agenda listed a public hearing on conduit financing for The RISE Block 5 Apartments Project, postponed from October 6, as well as an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement and the appointed employees' compensation program.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — October 20, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a special meeting of the Santa Clara City Council on October 20, 2026, at 5:30 pm, held in person at City Hall and virtually. Items before the Council included an update on the FIFA risk analysis disclosures investigation and several Council member requests to put future topics on the agenda, covering data centers and apartment parking.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an update on the FIFA Risk Analysis Disclosures Investigation.

Councilmember Hardy's request, deferred from October 6, asked for a staff update within 30 days on how new large electrical load uses, including data centers, get approvals and power allocation, with a possible moratorium on new stand-alone data centers.
Councilmember Hardy's request, also deferred from October 6, asked to discuss a policy that would bar the City from signing non-disclosure agreements with stand-alone data centers.
Councilmember Park's request, deferred from September 22 and October 6, asked to consider how apartment residents can park in or near their complexes without fear of being ticketed or towed.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine business like meeting calendars and past minutes, along with items on park design work, renaming of city garden and plaza spaces, and a mosquito control presentation. It also included the annual review of the city's advisory commissions and their plans for the coming year.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposed amendment of up to $130,000 with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for design services on the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park Project.

A resolution was listed to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden as the "Milpitas Community Garden" and Cesar Chavez Plaza as "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and to name the garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."
The Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District was listed to give a presentation to the Council.

The Council was scheduled to consider accepting the FY2025-26 annual report and approving FY2026-27 work plans for eight city commissions, including the Arts Commission, Economic Development and Trade Commission, and Library and Education Advisory Commission.

Routine items included the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, minutes from the October 6, 2026 meeting, a preview of items expected at the next regular meeting, and a list of items requested by Councilmembers.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda listed a public hearing before Palo Alto's Architectural Review Board on a request from AT&T to add new wireless equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles in the public right-of-way. The poles are near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue.
keyTopics: AT&T's request (file 26PLN-00229) to add new antennas, remote radio units, and associated equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles, treated as two Tier 2 wireless communication facilities
Proposed seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions on the poles, located near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Listed as a quasi-judicial public hearing, with the project marked exempt from environmental review under CEQA Section 15301 (Existing Facilities)
A supplemental report was added to the agenda packet for this item
